name: raxml-ng
desc: RAxML Next Generation: faster, easier-to-use and more flexible
why: Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree inference is real science you can run, though it is a specialist bioinformatics tool.

brief.what_it_is: RAxML-NG is a command-line phylogenetic tool that infers maximum-likelihood trees from a multiple sequence alignment. You give it an alignment (FASTA or similar via --msa) and a substitution model, and it searches for the best-scoring tree, optionally with bootstrap replicates, branch support values, or evaluation on a fixed topology. The output is tree files and run logs. It is the successor to RAxML 8 and is installed by the brew formula as the raxml-ng executable.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a faster, more flexible and more user-friendly successor to RAxML (Stamatakis 2014), and says it carries over features from ExaML such as checkpointing and load balancing for partitioned alignments.
brief.how_it_works: The search heuristic repeatedly applies Subtree Pruning and Regrafting (SPR) moves to climb toward the best-known maximum-likelihood tree. Likelihood computation uses the optimized coraxlib library. Version 2.0 adds adaptive search heuristics, automatic model selection (MOOSE), and fast branch support metrics, per the README.

brief.install_notes: Brew installs the binary directly. Upstream offers prebuilt zips for 64-bit Linux and macOS (version 2.0.3), and the README says Windows users can run the Linux binary under WSL with possibly lower performance. Building from source needs git with submodules and cmake; GMP and htslib (with htscodecs on Debian-based systems) are listed as dependencies. The README also lists coraxlib and terraphast as needed only for builds without submodules. There are PTHREADS, MPI and portable builds, plus an unstable dev branch. No account, runtime or configuration is mentioned.
brief.standout: It is a maintained successor to a well-known phylogenetics program, with newer features such as adaptive search, automatic model selection and fast support metrics. It also keeps a compatibility mode for the older v1.1.0 behaviour.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the README. It points to release 2.0.3 with downloadable binaries and describes version 2.0 features with DOIs dated 2023 to 2025. It notes that the primary repository has moved to Codeberg. I could not see a last-commit date on the pages I read, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage given in the brew metadata is the legacy RAxML 8 Exelixis Lab page, not the RAxML-NG project. Its download links are for old RAxML versions and the 'latest' link points to GitHub. The README says issues and pull requests belong on Codeberg. The code is licensed under AGPL-3.0, which matters for redistribution. It is a specialist bioinformatics tool that needs a multiple sequence alignment and some model knowledge to use well. Windows has no native build in the README.

entry.title: RAxML-NG
entry.tldr: Infers evolutionary trees from aligned DNA or protein sequences by maximum likelihood, the real method biologists use to work out who descends from whom.
entry.deeper_look:
RAxML-NG takes a multiple sequence alignment and a substitution model, then searches for the tree that makes the observed sequences most probable. It can also run bootstrap replicates, map support values onto a tree, or score a fixed topology. The output is tree files and run logs.

The search works by hill climbing. It starts from a tree, applies Subtree Pruning and Regrafting (SPR) moves, which cut a branch off and reattach it elsewhere, and keeps whatever improves the likelihood. The number of possible trees explodes as you add species, so the search is a heuristic and not a proof. Likelihood calculation is handled by a separate optimized library, coraxlib.

It is the successor to RAxML (Stamatakis 2014). The README describes it as faster, more flexible and more user-friendly, and says it carries over checkpointing and load balancing for partitioned alignments from ExaML. Version 2.0 adds adaptive search heuristics, automatic model selection (MOOSE) and fast branch support metrics.

The door it opens is phylogenetics itself: how substitution models, rate variation and bootstrap support turn a pile of sequences into a defensible family tree. You need an alignment to begin, and the project's wiki has a hands-on tutorial.

entry.whats_unique: It is a maintained successor to a well-known phylogenetics program, with adaptive search, automatic model selection and fast support metrics. It also keeps a compatibility mode for the older v1.1.0 behaviour.
entry.caveats: It is a specialist bioinformatics tool that needs an alignment and some model knowledge, the brew homepage points to the legacy RAxML 8 page, development lives on Codeberg, and the code is AGPL-3.0.
